notes.1: Most of the candidates answered this question correctly, ticking pen drive. There were only a few candidates that ticked two choices.
notes.2: On paper this was a straightforward book-type question although candidates found it challenging. Only part (c) being answered well. (a) (i) This was a very challenging question for many of the candidates. We were looking for what was meant by analogue data, namely that it was continuous data or was data in a waveform. However some candidates were vague in their answers stating that ‘it could not be read by a computer’ or ‘by a human’ therefore not answering the question. The Examiners did, however, allow appropriate examples of analogue data, but this may not be the case in future examinations. (ii) This again was a challenging question for most candidates. On paper both these questions were deemed to be straightforward, but candidates stated very general answers rather than specialist answers that stated that digital data was discrete data or binary data. As with part (i) some candidates wrote that this was ‘data that a computer could understand’ or ‘was stored digitally’. As with part (i) the Examiners allowed an example lik 0s and 1s, but this may not be the case in future series. (b) This was a new question that had never been asked in previous sessions of the examination. The Examiners thought that candidates would be able to give some good answers, but it was very challenging to many candidates. The Examiners were looking for was ‘to allow devices to be controlled’ or ‘to send to an actuator’. Candidates in the past found questions about measurement and control straightforward so we were surprised when candidates found this question challenging. Some candidates related the question back to part (i) and part (ii) answering that data was converted so that ‘it could be read by humans’. (c) This question used a list of answers where the candidates had to choose the correct answer. Many candidates were able to copy down the correct answer. One of two candidates either did not give answers from the list or merged answers. With merged answers the first part is marked then the rest ignored. (c) (i) This was well answered by the candidates. The correct answer was to #open the windows in the greenhouse’. The Examiners allowed slight deviations from the copying down of the words. (ii) This was well answered by many of the candidates although some answered with digital. (iii) This was well answered by many of the candidates with the correct answer being ‘measure acidity in the river’. Again as with part (i) the Examiners allowed slight deviations ion the copying down of the sentence.
notes.3: This was a challenging question for many of the candidates. This was a technical question that asked candidates to name three network communication devices. Some candidates misread network as mobile phone technology and therefore gave answers like smartphone, tablet and others gave WAN, LAN and WLAN. The answers we were looking for included switch, hub and router. Of the candidates that produced marks in this question they were able to name the device but had issues describing its use either muddling up the descriptions or writing a vague answer. 0417 Information and Communication Technology November 2023
notes.4: As with question 3 this also was a very challenging question for many candidates. This question asked candidates to name and describe appropriate validation checks for the named fields. The examination paper gave examples of the data contained in the fields to help point candidates in the right direction. Some candidates gave the correct validation check but then had issues with the description. Other candidates wrote down data from the field. The Examiners thought that this question would be straightforward as it contained elements from the practical paper. For those that gave the correct validation check many were vague with the description, for example Length check, the description was checking that up to 4 characters when the actual answer is exactly 4 characters or format check and then writing down dd/mm/yy rather than dd/mm/yyyy.
notes.5: This was a new topic for the examination even though phablet computers had been on the syllabus for quite some time. Some candidates understood the concept of the phablet computers but answered the question from their own knowledge meaning that answers were vague, and many found the question challenging. (a) A phablet computer is a smartphone and tablet computer hybrid. It is larger than a smartphone but smaller than a tablet computer but has the features of both devices. This is what the Examiners expected candidates to answer, however many found the question challenging. One of the main issues with technical topics like this one is that general names for devices of this type may be different from the technical name. For example the technical name is a smartphone, but candidates answer with phone which can be a mobile phone, a smartphone or other types of phones. (b) As with part (a) candidates found this question quite challenging. This question asked the candidates for advantages and disadvantages of a phablet rather than a smartphone and to relate it back to the project. An advantage and disadvantage must be a comparison answer, some candidates were simply answering as a statement and only giving one side of the answer. The candidates knew the difference but being vague in this way they could not gain all the mark available; the good answers included the facts that the screens were larger therefore the keyboards were larger. However if candidates had given an explanation why these were advantages, then other marks were available.

notes.7: This again was a challenging question with many candidates writing stateents rather than advantages and disadvantages. An advantage or disadvantage is a comparison therefore both sides of the argument are needed. Some candidates thought the quality of the video would diminish using a drone, whilst others misread the question and carried out a comparison with a human, rather than a human in a helicopter. notes.9: This again was a challenging question for many of the candidates. This question was a new variation on a topic that had been set many times. Candidates were asked to define both validation and verification and then explain why both were needed. Many candidates were able to pick up good marks by writing down examples of both validation and verification but there were a few instances where candidates wrote that verification checked for errors, but this is not the case it only checks that the data has been entered or copied correctly from the source document. Other candidates mixed up visual verification with proofreading which does not require a source document. Some candidates repeated the question when they answered it by writing validation checks to see if the data is valid or verification verifies the data. Less candidates could explain why both were needed. Some candidates thought that verification was related to checking the authenticity of a person and then validating who it was.
notes.10: This again was a challenging question for many of the candidates. (a) This was a standard book type question therefore should have been straightforward however many candidates found the question very challenging. The answers the Examiners were expecting included user requirements and hardware and software requirements. Some candidates knew the answer but missed out the type of system i.e. new or current. (b) This question allowed candidates to give some good answers although some candidates found the question quite hard. It involved an evaluation between parallel running and direct changeover. An evaluation involves positives and negatives of each type of implementation. Many candidates understood the concept of each type of implementation but did not give enough reasoning or descriptions to gain the higher marks. The Examiners allowed 2 marks for descriptions of both parallel running and direct changeover. In questions of this type it is important to expand on the answers given to ensure that higher marks can be awarded. Some candidates gave a good description of the different implementation methods but missed out the changeover for example parallel running involves to systems running side by side but missing out that the new system would take over. (c) This question related to using an online booking system rather than setting one up or the company operating it. Some good answers were given by the candidates, but they did not answer the question, therefore answers about saving money as they did not have to travel to the hotel to book could not gain marks as this may have been inappropriate as the hotel could have been in a different country. With questions that relate to a scenario candidates need to read the scenario before answering the question. Some candidates mixed up this with online shopping. (d) There were a number of different answers as to what WAN and WLAN were. Again this was a straightforward question that some candidates found difficult. A WAN is a Wide Area Network and a WLAN is a Wireless Local Area Network. Many candidates were able to name the networks but 0417 Information and Communication Technology November 2023 not expand upon this with good, detailed descriptions. For rxample a WAN covers a larger area than a WLAN is too vague, but it covers a larger geographical area makes it correct as it implies countrywide.
notes.11: Part (b) of this question was answered better than part (a) . the question was about internet shopping, which was not a new topic, but the style of the questions had not been set previously. (a) This question related to the benefits and drawbacks to the clothing retailer rather than the customer. In previous examinations the Examiners tended to ask question about the customer and this change of wording was missed by many candidates who answered the question with statements like ‘it would save time than going to the shop etc’. Some candidates started to answer about the retailer but added comments about the customer. There were some good answers given, like cost savings as fewer staff were required or more customers as it was worldwide and this would lead to higher profits, but again as in previous prose questions some of these lacked depth. (b) This part was answered better than part (a) and as there were so many possible answers many candidates were able to gain full marks.
